RFT Cluster-Level FWER

Source: R/rft.R
rft_cluster_fwer.Rd

Computes cluster-level FWER-corrected p-values using Random Field Theory cluster extent distribution.

Usage

rft_cluster_fwer(
  stat_vol,
  mask = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  tail = c("pos", "neg", "two"),
  cluster_thresh = 3,
  smoothness,
  df = Inf
)

Arguments

stat_vol

3D Z-equivalent statistic map (array or NeuroVol). Pass already-canonicalized input (use canonicalize() first for t-statistics or -log10(p) maps).

mask

Optional logical 3D mask. Defaults to finite voxels in stat_vol.

alpha

Significance level (default 0.05).

tail

One of "pos", "neg", "two". For "two", each direction uses alpha / 2 and the union is reported, targeting FWER alpha across both tails.

cluster_thresh

Cluster-forming threshold on the Z scale.

smoothness

A smoothness_fwhm() object specifying field smoothness in millimetres. Numeric input is also accepted (length 1 or 3, mm) and coerced internally.

df

Degrees of freedom. Use Inf for Gaussian field (Z-scores).

Value

A neurothresh_result with method = "rft_cluster_fwer". The clusters slot is the per-cluster table (id, size, p_unc, p_fwer, significant). threshold is cluster_thresh.

Details

First thresholds at cluster_thresh to form clusters, then tests each cluster's extent against the RFT null distribution. For tail = "two", the analysis runs separately on positive and negative tails at alpha / 2 and the union of significant clusters is reported. The reported p_fwer values are doubled (capped at 1) to describe the combined family; p_unc remains the one-tail cluster-extent probability.

Extent probabilities use a three-dimensional, high-threshold Gaussian approximation in dimensionless resels. This is an asymptotic baseline; changing physical units does not change its probabilities.

See also

rft_peak_fwer(), cluster_fdr().
